title: Brunswick session and recording contract
summary: Pollack arranges a Brunswick/Vocalion session with Fazola, Santo Pecora, Eddie Miller and Eddie Condon, which leads to a contract.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And he said, I'm glad you're in town. We're going to make some records with the big band and if you want to make a session, I'll be glad to arrange it for you.
What did I have to lose?
I said, well I'll be more than happy to. So he got me a date and it was with Brunswick. That's right, Brunswick. They made another label called Vocalion.
Yeah, I remember those black label vocalions, gold printing on them.

So we got Farz, Ben Pollack was on the drums, Santo Pecora played the trombone, and Eddie Miller played the sax. Eddie Condon played the guitar. And a fellow by the name of Al Hort was a piano player, a Negro, but he was a fine piano player. So to make a long story short, we made a session, and we made a good session at that time, and I got a contract.

So I got a contract to record for Brunswick, which held me over in New York. I didn't have nothing to worry about then, and then I got paid, you know, and I got a little royalty. So I stayed in New York, and Nick Rangetti, the place that I played in the village, he knew about me. He didn't know me, but he knew about me through a fellow by the name of Sidney Harriton. Oh yeah. You remember him? I never knew him. He had died before I got there.
